title: U.S. House · California's 17th Congressional District
area: Parts of Santa Clara and Alameda counties in Silicon Valley, including Fremont, Newark, Santa Clara, Milpitas, and parts of San Jose.

context.text: California redrew its congressional district lines for the 2026 elections under Proposition 50, a mid-decade redistricting measure voters approved in a November 2025 special election.
In the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, Ro Khanna won 62.3% of the vote (83,051 votes) and Ritesh Tandon won 14.8% (19,793 votes), advancing them both to the November general election.

summary.text: Ro Khanna is the Democratic incumbent for California's 17th District in Silicon Valley, serving his fifth term. A former attorney, university lecturer and Commerce Department official, he first ran for the seat in 2014, lost to then-Rep. Mike Honda, and defeated Honda in 2016. His House website lists him on the Armed Services and Oversight committees and as a member of the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party.

background.text: Born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, in 1976 (September 13, per Wikipedia).
Earned a bachelor's degree in economics from the University of Chicago in 1998 and a J.D. from Yale University in 2001.

Worked as an attorney; in 2009 President Barack Obama appointed him a deputy assistant secretary at the U.S. Department of Commerce, where he led trade missions. He left in 2011 to join the law firm Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati.

Taught as a visiting lecturer in economics at Stanford University (2012-2016) and taught law at Santa Clara University; published a 2012 book on American competitiveness, Entrepreneurial Nation. Ballotpedia also lists membership on the California Workforce Development Board.
Ran for the 17th District seat in 2014, losing to Rep. Mike Honda 51.8% to 48.2% in the general election, then defeated Honda in the 2016 general election.
Took office in January 2017 and is serving his fifth term, per his House website.

Serves on the House Armed Services Committee (ranking member of the Subcommittee on Cyber, Innovative Technologies and Information Systems), the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition between the U.S. and the Chinese Communist Party, and the Oversight and Accountability Committee, where he previously chaired the Environment Subcommittee.

priorities.text: Lists an innovation-driven, diversified economy as a priority, including advanced manufacturing, high-tech apprenticeships and worker training, and boosting clean steel manufacturing.

Says expanding affordable child care is a priority, citing his role as a co-founder of the Congressional Bipartisan Affordable Childcare Caucus working toward $10-per-day child care with family-supporting wages for child-care workers.
Lists protecting Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid, and lowering prescription drug costs, as priorities for health care and the social safety net.

positions.summary: Supports a woman's right to choose and access to affordable health care.
positions.quote: I support a woman's right to choose and I will continue to push for accessible and affordable health care for all.

positions.summary: Supports requiring background checks for all gun sales and voted for a federal assault weapons ban.
positions.quote: Congress should also pass a federal assault weapons ban, which I was proud to vote for in the House.

positions.summary: Has introduced resolutions calling for reform and oversight of ICE and CBP conduct, and supports pathways to legal status rather than broader enforcement.
positions.quote: Undocumented immigrants contribute to American society and we must protect their legal rights and status. I will advocate for legal status for DREAMers, pathways to citizenship for productive adults, family reunification visas, guest worker visa programs, and asylum for refugees.

positions.summary: Supports creating a single-payer health care system (Medicare for All) to expand coverage and lower costs.
positions.quote: I support the creation of a single-payer health care system, or Medicare for All. We must increase coverage, support small businesses, expand primary care, and lower premiums.

positions.summary: Supports repealing fossil fuel subsidies, closing fracking loopholes, and banning fracking on public lands as part of a shift to renewable energy.
positions.quote: I support legislation to repeal fossil fuel subsidies and close loopholes for fracking that exempt Big Oil companies from clean water and air regulations. I also support a ban on fracking on public lands.

positions.summary: Supports funding to help law enforcement do their jobs and has backed legislation investing in community policing and hiring capacity.
positions.quote: I have been proud to support bipartisan legislation to invest in community policing and support increasing funding and hiring capacity.

positions.summary: Supports raising the hourly minimum wage to at least $17 per hour.
positions.quote: I also support paid family leave, training programs for mid-career workers, and increasing the hourly minimum wage to at least $17 per hour.

record.text: Serves on the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Government Innovation; Economic Growth, Energy Policy, and Regulatory Affairs subcommittees), and the House Committee on Armed Services (Cyber Information Technologies and Innovation; Seapower and Projection Forces subcommittees) in the 119th Congress.
Introduced the End ICE Abuse Resolution asserting Congress's authority over immigration enforcement funding and calling for oversight of federal immigration agencies.
Co-authored the CHIPS and Science Act, which funds domestic semiconductor manufacturing.
Introduced the American Housing and Economic Mobility Act, which would leverage federal funding to build up to 3.2 million new housing units for lower-income and middle-class families.
Was an original cosponsor of the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act, which included his PEACE Act provisions to ban chokeholds and no-knock warrants.

candidates.name: Ritesh Tandon
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2 top-two primary with 14.8% of the vote

summary.text: Ritesh Tandon is an engineer and business executive who has been the Republican candidate for California's 17th District before: he finished second to Rep. Ro Khanna in the general elections of 2020 and 2022, and ran in the 2024 primary as a Democrat. He was the lead plaintiff in Tandon v. Newsom, a 2021 U.S. Supreme Court case on COVID-19 restrictions on religious gatherings. His 2026 Ballotpedia survey describes affordability, public safety and education as priorities.

background.text: Describes himself as coming to the United States from India at age 28 and as a Silicon Valley resident for two decades, per his Ballotpedia survey.
Earned a B.S. in mechanical engineering from L.D. College of Engineering in India, and an M.S. in computer engineering and an M.B.A. from Santa Clara University.

Worked on unified communications products at Cisco, starting in engineering and moving into technical marketing, and later managed global strategic alliances at Jabra, per his 2022 Ballotpedia survey; his 2026 survey says he spent 24 years in the tech industry before founding his own company.
Is CEO of Kricel Corporation and a research fellow at UC Berkeley's Haas School of Business.
Has served as chief liaison officer for the Smart Village Movement and as vice-chairman of UPMA, and on the executive committee of the Sankara Eye Foundation.
Was the named plaintiff in Tandon v. Newsom, in which the U.S. Supreme Court on April 9, 2021 granted, 5-4, an injunction against California limits on at-home religious gatherings.

Ran against Khanna as the Republican in the 2020 general election (28.7%) and 2022 general election (29.1%); in the March 2024 primary he appeared on the ballot as a Democrat and received 4.9%, not advancing.

priorities.text: Lists affordability as a top priority, saying CA-17 families are 'squeezed by rent, gas, groceries, and healthcare,' and calls for lowering housing, healthcare, and prescription-drug costs and opposing a state wealth tax and mileage tax.
Says he wants to 'bring jobs back to California' by simplifying small-business taxes, easing regulation, and fast-tracking permits for data centers, semiconductors, and advanced manufacturing.
Calls for 8-year congressional term limits, a ban on congressional stock trading, securing the border, and enforcing voter ID.

positions.summary: Supports securing the border with technology and enforcement and ending 'catch-and-release.'
positions.quote: Secure the border with modern technology, anti-cartel ops, and rapid processing. End catch-and-release.

positions.summary: Opposes California's proposed wealth tax and a mileage tax, and calls for cutting taxes generally.
positions.quote: Stop tax-and-fee overload — oppose CA's wealth tax and mileage tax.

positions.summary: Says education funding should follow the child regardless of whether the school is public, charter, or a parent's choice.
positions.quote: Fund the child, not the bureaucracy — public, charter, or parents' choice.

positions.summary: Calls for federal incentives for new housing supply and first-time homebuyer support to address affordability.

record.text: Was the named plaintiff in Tandon v. Newsom (2021), in which the U.S. Supreme Court ruled 5-4 that California's COVID-19 restrictions on at-home religious gatherings likely violated the First Amendment.
